# Mixing Tank: Functional Narrative and Upgrade Findings

This is based only on the rung export and the technician's notes. Items marked **[VERIFY]** are assumptions about polarity or field wiring that the logic alone can't confirm. Please check them before the FDS is issued.

---

## Part 1: Functional Narrative (Existing System)

### 1.1 Overview

The tank system has one run/stop state. While it is running, it:

- keeps the tank filled to the high-level switch,
- agitates when there is enough level, and
- heats with steam to a discrete temperature switch setpoint.

There is no batch sequence, recipe, drain control or analog measurement in this logic. The only alarm is a fill timeout.

### 1.2 I/O Summary

| Tag | Address | Type | Description / Polarity |
|---|---|---|---|
| START_PB | I:1/0 | DI | Start pushbutton (NO, momentary). Also resets the fill-timeout alarm. |
| STOP_PB | I:1/1 | DI | Stop pushbutton, NC. ON = healthy. |
| ESTOP_OK | I:1/2 | DI | E-stop chain status. ON = healthy. **[VERIFY whether this is a hardwired safety relay status or the E-stop contact itself]** |
| LSL_TANK | I:1/3 | DI | Low-level switch. **ON = level above low point** (per technician). |
| LSH_TANK | I:1/4 | DI | High-level switch. Assumed ON = level at/above high point. **[VERIFY]** |
| AGIT_HAND | I:1/5 | DI | Panel-door selector, "Hand" position. |
| TEMP_LOW | I:1/6 | DI | Temperature switch. Assumed ON = temperature below setpoint. **[VERIFY]** |
| FILL_VLV | O:2/0 | DO | Fill valve open command. **[VERIFY fail position]** |
| AGITATOR | O:2/1 | DO | Agitator motor run command. |
| STEAM_VLV | O:2/2 | DO | Steam valve open command. **[VERIFY fail position]** |
| ALARM_HORN | O:2/3 | DO | Audible alarm. |
| RUN_LATCH | B3:0/0 | Internal | System running state. |
| T4:0 | — | RTO | Fill timeout, 600 s preset, retentive. |

### 1.3 Run / Stop Control (R0)

- The operator presses **START** to put the system in RUN. RUN is held in by a seal-in.
- RUN drops out when **STOP** is pressed or the **E-stop** chain opens. When either is restored, RUN does **not** resume until START is pressed again.
- **Observed behavior:** RUN has been seen to come back on after a power cycle with no START press. See Finding 1.

### 1.4 Fill Control (R1, R2)

- While RUN is active, the fill valve opens whenever the high-level switch is not made and the fill timeout has not expired.
- The valve closes when the high-level switch makes. It reopens when the switch clears, so it tops up whenever level falls below the switch for any reason.
- A retentive timer (T4:0) accumulates time whenever the fill valve is open. When the total reaches 600 s, the fill valve is locked closed and the horn sounds.
- The timer is **not** reset at the end of a fill, on stop, or on power-up. It resets **only** when START is pressed.

### 1.5 Agitation (R3)

The agitator runs while RUN is active and either of these is true:

- **(Auto)** level is above the low-level switch, or
- **(Hand)** the panel-door selector is in Hand.

In Hand, the low-level permissive is ignored. RUN is still required, so "Hand" is really a low-level bypass rather than an independent manual mode.

### 1.6 Heating (R4)

- The steam valve opens while the agitator is **commanded** on and the temperature switch indicates low.
- Control is on/off around the switch setpoint. There is no analog temperature, no high-temperature limit and no agitator run feedback.

### 1.7 Alarms (R5, R6)

| Alarm | Trigger | Action | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fill timeout | T4:0 accumulated ≥ 600 s | Fill valve held closed, horn on. Agitator and steam continue. | START pushbutton |

There is no separate acknowledge or silence. No other abnormal condition is alarmed.

---

## Part 2: Behavior That Should Not Be Carried Forward

Ordered roughly by risk.

### 1. Uncommanded restart after power loss (R0) — **High**

- The technician saw RUN come back after a power cycle and the tank start filling. The same restart would also start the **agitator** (if level is above LSL) and **steam** (if temperature is low), with nobody at the panel.
- SLC-500 data tables are retentive. A seal-in that reads its own retained bit on the first scan can re-establish itself if STOP and E-stop are healthy.
- **[VERIFY]** whether another cause contributes: a latch elsewhere in the program, a sticking START contact, or files missing from the export.
- **Upgrade requirement:** after a power loss or controller restart, the system powers up in STOPPED, and a deliberate operator START is needed. Also make START edge-triggered so a welded or held button cannot cause a restart.

### 2. Hand selector bypasses the low-level interlock and lets steam in on a low tank (R3 → R4) — **High**

- In Hand, the agitator runs with the impeller possibly uncovered. That risks seal and gearbox damage, plus vibration.
- Steam is permitted on the agitator *command*, so Hand also allows **steam into a tank below the low-level point**. That risks exposed jacket or coil heating, scorching product, and thermal stress.
- The selector sits on the panel door, so anyone can operate it, and nothing records that it was used.
- **Upgrade requirement:** the low-level permissive for steam must be independent of agitator mode. If a maintenance jog or bypass is truly needed, it should be access-controlled, time-limited, alarmed and logged, and it must never permit steam.

### 3. Steam interlocked to agitator command, not proven running — **Medium-High**

- If the agitator trips on overload, or a contactor fails, steam keeps flowing into a stagnant tank.
- **Upgrade requirement:** steam needs proven agitator running (an auxiliary contact or VFD run status), proven level, and an independent high-temperature limit.

### 4. No high-temperature protection — **Medium-High**

- The only temperature input is a low switch. If it fails in the "low" state, or the steam valve sticks open, nothing stops overheating.
- **Upgrade requirement:** use an analog temperature for control, plus an independent high-temperature cutout. Decide whether that cutout must be hardwired, based on the hazard assessment.

### 5. Overfill protection relies on a single, possibly non-fail-safe switch — **Medium-High**

- The fill valve opens when LSH is *not* made. If LSH is ON-when-high, a broken wire or failed switch looks like "not full" and fill continues until the 600 s cumulative timer runs out.
- **Upgrade requirement:** confirm LSH is wired fail-safe (de-energized = high). Add an independent high-high switch that closes fill directly, and ideally an analog level for control.
- LSL already appears fail-safe (OFF = low), which is good. Keep that convention and rename the tag so it states its polarity, for example `LSL_TANK_COVERED`.

### 6. Fill timeout logic is ineffective (R2, R6) — **Medium**

- **The timer accumulates across every top-up and never resets on fill completion.** Normal operation will eventually trip it, so the trip doesn't mean any single fill was slow.
- **It resets only on START.** An operator can press START at any time, even while running, to clear the timer and reopen the valve. That defeats the protection.
- **Reset and restart are the same action.** Clearing the alarm also re-enables filling into whatever caused the timeout, such as a leak, a failed level switch or an open drain.
- **Upgrade requirement:** time each fill individually, resetting when the high level is reached. The timeout should latch a fault that stops filling, and it must need a separate acknowledge or reset before fill can resume.

### 7. Fill valve chatter at high level — **Low-Medium**

- The valve has no deadband, so it cycles every time the level bounces at LSH, from agitation or waves. That wears the valve and causes water hammer.
- **Upgrade requirement:** fill to high and don't refill until level drops by a defined amount (analog level), or add a time-based debounce.

### 8. E-stop implemented as a PLC input only — **[VERIFY], potentially High**

- The logic shows ESTOP_OK only as a permissive in the run latch. If that is the *only* way the E-stop acts, it does not meet ISO 13850 / NFPA 79 / IEC 60204-1 expectations. E-stop must remove energy through hardwired or safety-rated means, independent of the standard PLC program.
- **Upgrade requirement:** a safety relay or safety controller drops the motor contactor and de-energizes the valve solenoids. The PLC monitors status only.

### 9. Minimal alarming and no diagnostics — **Medium**

- E-stop trips, agitator faults, level switch discrepancies (such as LSH made while LSL not made) and temperature faults all go unannounced.
- There is no horn silence separate from reset.
- **Upgrade requirement:** follow ISA-18.2 practice, with distinct alarms, acknowledge/silence, and first-out where useful.

---

## Part 3: Open Items to Resolve Before Finalizing the FDS

1. Confirm the polarity of LSH_TANK and TEMP_LOW, and the fail positions of the fill and steam valves.
2. Confirm how the E-stop is actually wired: hardwired removal of power, or the PLC input only.
3. Confirm the export is complete: all ladder files, any S:1/15 first-scan logic, and any latch/unlatch instructions on B3:0/0.
4. Find out how the tank is drained and emptied. Nothing in this logic handles it.
5. Establish the process intent: continuous hold-and-heat or batch? That determines whether the new system should keep "fill-to-high continuously" or move to a sequenced batch.
6. Ask operations what AGIT_HAND is actually used for, so a controlled replacement can be specified rather than just removed.
